title: SEBI's Mutual Fund-Only PMS: A New Era for Wealth Advisers?
description: SEBI has proposed a new framework for Portfolio Management Services (PMS) focused exclusively on mutual funds. This initiative aims to make professional portf.

faq.q: What is a Portfolio Management Service (PMS)?
faq.a: A PMS is a professional service where a fund manager manages a client's investment portfolio, typically consisting of stocks, bonds, and other securities. It offers a personalised approach, often for high-net-worth individuals, with a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh under current regulations.

faq.q: How is a mutual fund-only PMS different from a regular PMS?
faq.a: A regular PMS can invest directly in various securities, including stocks. A mutual fund-only PMS, as proposed by SEBI, would exclusively invest client funds in direct plans of mutual fund schemes, including ETFs and SIFs, and would have a lower minimum investment threshold of ₹25 lakh.

faq.q: Will this new framework replace RIAs or MFDs?
faq.a: No, it is not intended to replace RIAs or MFDs but rather to offer an additional, distinct service category. It provides an opportunity for existing advisers to expand their offerings, though MFDs opting for MF-PMS will need to maintain strict client segregation and an arm's length relationship between their distribution and management activities.

faq.q: What are the main benefits for investors from a mutual fund-only PMS?
faq.a: Investors can benefit from professional management of their mutual fund portfolios, access to direct plans (potentially leading to lower costs), and a lower entry barrier (₹25 lakh) compared to traditional PMS. It offers a structured way to achieve diversification and aligns adviser incentives with portfolio growth.

faq.q: What are the key challenges for financial advisers in adopting this model?
faq.a: Advisers will face significant compliance demands, including a minimum net worth requirement of ₹2 crore, separate SEBI registration, and stringent operational complexities like client-level segregation and maintaining an arm's length relationship for MFDs. These hurdles may be particularly challenging for smaller advisory firms.

faq.q: When is this proposal expected to be implemented?
faq.a: The proposal is currently in the consultation paper stage, meaning SEBI is seeking public comments and views. The final regulations will be issued after this consultation process, so an exact implementation timeline is not yet available but typically takes several months.
